Project Wings · A playbook for friends and family

How long can you be self-sufficient at home?

A creative, measured test of off-grid living at home, using gear you already have, to find the real limit, not to guess it. This is a test, not an emergency plan.

Start here Water Food Heat and cooking Power Comms and maps Security / sanitation / barter / network / printing

Action: read the safety rules below before anything else.

What this is: a measured test of off-grid living at home. What it is not: an emergency plan.

Safety first, non-negotiable

  • Ventilate, always, when a propane stove or heater is running. Never run one in a closed room.
  • Never sleep with a propane heater running.
  • Working carbon monoxide detector with fresh batteries, in the room where propane is used.
  • If the CO alarm sounds, or you feel headache, nausea, or dizziness: stop, ventilate, and get out.

Propane: safe handling and storage, for anyone

Propane basics, in plain words: propane is the fuel that comes in metal tanks. Used the right way, it is safe. The three rules in the red box above come first, then the storage and use tips below.

  • Store propane outdoors, upright, in a ventilated area, away from heat and ignition. Never store cylinders in living spaces, basements, or near exits or stairways.
  • Check your appliance manual for the cylinder type it takes. Some stoves can run from a larger tank with an adapter hose (about $15 to $20), but that use may be outside your stove manual. Some heaters cannot connect to a bulk tank at all.
  • Look for ODS (oxygen depletion sensor) and tip-over shut-off on any indoor-safe heater.
  • Check your local fire code before storing any tank. Rules vary by place and building type, and the local code is the final word.
  • Cold storage: treat -40°F as the low end for storing cylinders. Propane stops vaporizing at -44°F, and a small cylinder can lose usable pressure well before that, especially below 0°F.

A note on local rules: Check your local rules now, while services are normal. In a true emergency when you cannot rely on government services, use your own judgment, and follow the law.

Water solutions

Action: do your drinking math: gallons on hand divided by gallons per day.

  • Drinking runs about 0.5 to 1 gallon a day, plus cooking and hygiene. Do the math for your supply: gallons on hand divided by gallons per day equals days. Drinking only stretches furthest. Realistic use, drinking plus cooking and hygiene, goes faster. Comfortable use goes fastest.
  • Extra jugs only if you want to test longer than your current supply covers.

Checked. One small filter: Sawyer MINI.

What it is: a small personal squeeze filter. What it is not: a household gravity system, and Sawyer does not claim virus removal for it.

Specs: 2 ounces field weight, rated up to 100,000 gallons, 0.1 micron. For a household, pair it with a gravity bag or pick a larger gravity filter.

This matches the earlier note about a filter near $30 rated near 100,000 gallons. Maker page price checked at $28.99. Check the maker page for the current price.

Food solutions

Action: count calories for one day of stored food.

  • Stored food, about 2,000 calories a day: rice, oats, beans, canned meat or fish, canned vegetables, peanut butter, shelf-stable milk, salt, oil, coffee or tea if you want it.
  • Sprouts: good for quick food, grow in a very small space.
  • Food sealers: canned food sealers or vacuum sealers.

Checked. 4Patriots 4-Week Survival Food Kit.

What it is: a kit with 186 servings and 36,520 calories. What it is not: a complete 2,000-calorie replacement.

Correction that matters: at the maker's own math of about 1,304 calories a day for one person, this lasts about 18 days at a full 2,000 calories a day, not four weeks. It needs about 9.25 gallons of filtered water to prepare. Shelf life is 25 years under proper storage.

No price shown here; the page excerpt checked did not list one. See the maker page for the current price.

See the 4-week food kit

What it is: the maker page for the 4-Week Survival Food Kit. What it is not: four weeks at full calories; at 2,000 calories a day it is about 18 days.

Heat and cooking

Action: check your heater and stove manuals.

  • Check your heater manual for hours per cylinder. Cylinder type: see Start here. Plan heat fuel separately from cooking fuel.
  • Fire-starting tools: electric lighter, and a magnifying glass to start fires with sun / solar.

Power

Action: write down your station numbers.

Plain words first: how much power it holds, how strong the output is, and what a panel can and cannot do.

Solar Panels and Batteries

  • How much power it holds, in watt-hours, and how strong the output is, in watts. Fill them in on the Phase 0 checklist in My plan.
  • Check each appliance's watts against the output limit. Do not run appliances together if their combined watts exceed the limit.
  • Small portable panels charge slowly. Expect slow charging, not a full house system.
  • Log real runtimes and real solar input in Phase 1. Do not quote them until they are measured.

Comms and maps

Action: download your maps while you have internet.

  • Physical maps, plus downloaded maps on a phone.
  • Radios that can tune in weather alerts and similar.
  • Hand-crank / solar NOAA weather radio for true off-grid news and weather. No verified product link yet; none is listed here.

Checked. MeshCore.

What it is not: a phone. What it is: firmware plus a separate LoRa companion radio paired to a phone by Bluetooth, with repeaters doing the relaying. In short: phone plus radio plus app, and repeaters are what give it range. A visitor who buys only an app will get nowhere.

Setup uses the USA/Canada Recommended preset, 910.525 MHz. Radios range about $13 to hundreds, many $30 to $80. Comparison: Meshtastic relays at every node, max 7 hops. MeshCore relays only at repeaters, up to 64 hops, and companions do not rebroadcast.

No specific radio model picked. Model choice: Still checking, needs approval.

See the MeshCore setup guide

What it is: step-by-step setup for the USA/Canada preset. What it is not: a radio to buy; you still need a companion radio.

See the MeshCore web flasher

What it is: the browser tool that installs MeshCore firmware. What it is not: a substitute for reading the setup guide.

See MeshCore vs Meshtastic

What it is: a comparison of how relaying works. What it is not: a buying recommendation.

The catch: phone radio apps are internet streams. They do not work off grid without cell or wifi, and the phone has no FM tuner. Options that need internet: TuneIn (biggest catalog, news and sports, free with ads), the Radio tab built into the phone (free, no subscription), and the NOAA Weather Radio app (200+ National Weather Service broadcasts, push alerts, about $4.99). None of these work off grid.

My plan

Action: fill in the Phase 0 checklist.

Fill in your own numbers. Nothing here is pre-filled.

Phases

Each phase earns the next one. No skipping on enthusiasm.

Phase 0 · One evening

Audit

List, with numbers, everything on the Phase 0 checklist below.

Buy only what the audit shows missing.

Phase 1 · 24 hours

First test

Grid off for lights, cooking, and water use, as far as safely possible. Keep the fridge and phone charger as the control group, or note them as grid use. Log water, propane, battery, and meals every few hours. See Daily log below for the template.

Phase 2 · 72 hours

The real test

Same rules, longer. This is where water and food math gets real. See Water solutions and Food solutions. Stop early if safety, sleep, or work is affected.

Phase 3 · 7 days, only if Phase 2 was clean

Full week

Only after a clean 72 hours, with enough water and food bought in, and no safety flags.

Phase 0 checklist

  • Battery station: watt-hours (Wh) and AC output limit (W), written down.See Solar Panels and Batteries for what each number means.
  • Solar panel watts, written down.See Solar Panels and Batteries.
  • Propane tank size and count, written down.See Start here for storage rules.
  • Adapter hose, yes or no, confirmed.Needed only if running a larger tank. See Start here.
  • CO detector, yes or no, with fresh batteries, in the room where propane is used.See Start here.
  • Food on hand, counted by calories.See Food solutions for the daily target.
  • Water containers, counted.See Water solutions for the drinking math.
  • Phone and light charging needs, listed.
  • Camping gear, full list audited.Do not assume contents.
